name: manual_9f3386
claim: A repo-wide banned-term grep in a policy doc (e.g. reject unauthorized use of a reserved word like coordinator) false-positives on vendored dependency code that happens to contain the same substring for unrelated reasons -- e.g. a Python virtualenv's bundled pygments lexer listing Apple Cocoa API class names ending in Coordinator is not a policy violation. Fix: scope the check to git ls-files (tracked files only, excluding untracked dependency directories by construction) instead of a plain recursive grep with manually maintained exclude flags -- more robust because it can't be defeated by a new dependency directory the exclude list doesn't yet know about.

decisions.notes: Hit while hardening the coordinator-vs-orchestrator acceptance-check grep in orama-system's unified absorption plan doc (PR #280 round 2): a recursive grep matched a vendored lexer file before an exclude-dir fix was added; switching the coordinator check specifically to a tracked-files-only listing piped into grep sidesteps the whole class of dependency-directory false positives rather than chasing them one exclude flag at a time.
